question: Why do nurses collect data when doing research?

options.A: Fulfilling statutory requirements for medical licensure
options.B: Reducing the overall duration of hospital admissions
options.C: Increasing the administrative workload of hospital staff
options.D: Gathering information to support evidence-based practice

explanation: Data collection provides the facts needed to improve patient care standards and clinical methods. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h1)

question: Why should you clearly define your study variables before starting research?

options.A: To shorten the writing phase of the final manuscript
options.B: To eliminate the need for ethical board approval
options.C: To ensure the collected data aligns with the research purpose
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing equipment

explanation: Clear definitions prevent you from gathering irrelevant information and keep your study focused. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of collecting primary data?

options.A: Reviewing patient admission registers from the previous year
options.B: Analyzing past mortality statistics from a government bulletin
options.C: Reading a published review article in a nursing journal
options.D: Administering a new questionnaire directly to surgical patients

explanation: Primary data is collected directly by you from the source population for your current study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of using secondary data instead of primary data?
explanation: Using existing records saves you the time and resources needed to recruit participants and take new measurements. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which tool is best for collecting physical measurements like blood pressure?
explanation: Biophysical instruments give you objective numerical values like vital signs. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h3)

question: A researcher wants to watch and record how often nurses wash their hands. Which tool works best?
explanation: Structured checklists let observers systematically record specific actions like hand hygiene compliance. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h3)

question: In qualitative research, what does 'data saturation' mean?

options.A: The researcher has run out of financial funding
options.B: All participants have completed their survey forms
options.C: No new themes or information emerge from participants
options.D: The audio recording equipment has reached full capacity

explanation: Saturation means you have heard enough repetition and depth to stop interviewing further people. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h4)

question: Why are focus group discussions helpful in qualitative studies?

options.A: They provide precise numerical scores for statistical evaluation
options.B: They eliminate the need for audio recording devices during sessions
options.C: They prevent dominant participants from steering the conversation
options.D: They allow interaction and debate among participants to reveal shared views

explanation: Group dynamics spark discussions and bring out common beliefs that single interviews might miss. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h4)

question: What does 'reliability' mean when talking about a research tool?

options.A: The degree to which the tool measures the intended concept
options.B: Consistency and stability of the measurement results over time
options.C: The approval rating of the tool by an ethical committee
options.D: How easily participants can complete the data form

explanation: Reliability means if you repeat the measurement under the same conditions, you get similar results. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h5)

question: How do researchers make sure different data collectors get the same results?

options.A: By eliminating the need for pilot testing the instruments
options.B: By allowing each collector to use their own personal style
options.C: By training all collectors on standardized data gathering procedures
options.D: By reducing the sample size to a single investigator

explanation: Standard training ensures every observer interprets signs and records information in the exact same way. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h5)

question: Which action best protects a patient's privacy during data collection?

options.A: Storing completed interview transcripts in an unlocked office drawer
options.B: Discussing clinical findings openly in the hospital cafeteria
options.C: Including patient home addresses in the final published paper
options.D: Replacing patient names on forms with unique identification codes

explanation: Coding removes personal identifiers from the research records to protect patient privacy. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h6)

question: Why must you get informed consent before collecting data from a patient?

options.A: Preventing participants from asking questions about the study
options.B: Ensuring participants understand the study and agree voluntarily
options.C: Guarantying that participants receive financial compensation
options.D: Fulfilling a legal formality to speed up hospital discharge

explanation: Informed consent respects patient autonomy by making sure they know what the study involves before joining. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h6)

question: Why do a pilot test before starting your main research study?

options.A: Identifying and fixing problems with the data collection tools
options.B: Eliminating the requirement for institutional ethical review
options.C: Publishing the final research paper ahead of schedule
options.D: Recruiting the entire target population for the main study

explanation: A pilot test helps you spot confusing questions or mistakes in your plan before the real study starts. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h7)

question: During a pilot test, people keep getting confused by question four. What should you do?

options.A: Revise and clarify the wording of question four
options.B: Ignore the confusion and proceed with the main study
options.C: Delete the question without making any adjustments
options.D: Scold the participants for lacking comprehension skills

explanation: Feedback from a pilot test is meant to help you fix unclear questions so your data stays accurate. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h7)

question: Which step is essential for keeping digital research files safe?

options.A: Using encrypted files and strong password protection
options.B: Sharing login passwords freely among all project staff
options.C: Storing raw data exclusively on personal social media apps
options.D: Leaving computers logged in at nursing workstations

explanation: Encryption and passwords keep unauthorized people from opening sensitive research files. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h8)

question: Why is keeping a clear chain of custody important for research data?

options.A: It eliminates the need for ethical board oversight
options.B: It tracks who handled the data and prevents unauthorized access
options.C: It automatically analyzes qualitative text files into themes
options.D: It reduces the time required to write the reference list

explanation: A chain of custody proves who looked after the data, keeping the information secure and trustworthy. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h8)
